Walmart announces it will officially start supporting Apple Pay next week. Despite ongoing pressure from consumers, the retailer has refused to offer Apple Pay for years.

Apple Pay finally lands at Walmart

Walmart announced the news today via a press release. Starting August 24, the company will roll out contactless payment—including Apple Pay—at select Walmart and Sam's Club locations. The feature will expand to all stores across the US by the end of this year and reach fuel stations by mid-2027.

Walmart is bringing on full contactless payment support, including Apple Pay on iPhone and Apple Watch, Google Pay, contactless credit and debit cards, and other payment platforms. Customers can also add their Walmart and Sam's Club membership cards to Apple Wallet and other platforms. Contactless payment will operate alongside existing payment methods, including Walmart Pay.

The company stated:

Walmart was one of the last major retailers still not supporting Apple Pay, making this big news for consumers. For years, the retailer had refused to offer contactless payment and insisted on pushing its own QR-code-based payment system, Walmart Pay.

Until last year, Walmart still firmly believed Walmart Pay offered customers a more convenient experience than Apple Pay. However, to use Walmart Pay, users had to first add a credit or debit card within the Walmart app on iPhone, then scan a QR code at checkout to complete payment.

A quick search on social media reveals plenty of users expressing strong frustration over Walmart's refusal to support Apple Pay.

After all, most other retailers that had long refused Apple Pay—such as Kroger, Home Depot, and H-E-B—had given in years ago.

Does Walmart's lack of Apple Pay support affect your shopping habits? Now that Apple Pay is coming to Walmart and Sam's Club, will you be more inclined to shop there? Let us know in the comments.
